hints: A centroid is a node whose removal leaves no component containing more than n/2 nodes.
Root the tree and compute subtree sizes.
A node is a centroid when every child subtree is at most n/2 and the parent-side remainder is at most n/2.
analogy: Remove one node and check whether any remaining piece holds more than half the tree.
example: In a 7-node path, the middle node leaves components of sizes 3 and 3, so it is a centroid.
algorithm: Compute subtree sizes in one DFS. For each node, take the maximum of n-subtreeSize[u] and all child subtree sizes; print u if this maximum<=n/2.
correctness: The components after removing u are exactly its child subtrees plus the parent-side remainder; checking their largest size is the defining condition.
